Tolkein directly addresses this in one of his letters. No - The One Ring does not grant desires. It prevents life from ending, it gives a person access to the craftiness and subterfuge they already possess, and it adds its own will to the powers that they already have.

It is not a magic lamp - it would not have fulfilled their wishes, but it also would not necessarily have made them invisible. At least, not at first. But in time? If they did not master the Ring, it would master them, and they would eventually disappear completely - becoming Ring Wraiths (which are permanently insubstantial and totally bodiless).

Remember that the Ring did not just make Frodo invisible. It also gave him the power to command Gollum, and to make Gollum fulfill his oaths, and to suffer whenever he thought of breaking them. Sam himself recognized that Frodo always had this something greater in himself: a sort of gift to seem important to others, and that it started to become greater around the time that they were drawing near Faramir's group.
